title: Commentary on the Octateuch and Kings
english: Commentaries on the Octateuch and on the Kings, a series of fifty-one memoirs on the Octateuch and the books of Kings, having already been first published in print, deserves indeed the most pious and most serene ruler of all Wallachia, Lord Gregory Alexander Gica; and [produced] by the care of Nikephoros, hieromonk of the Theotokos. In Leipzig of Saxony, in the typography of Breitkopf. Year 1858.

Chapter 1, verse 14. And God said, 'Let there be lights in the expanse of the heaven for the purpose of the earth, to divide between the day and between the night' (Genesis 1:14). Didymus. Therefore also the lights, having come into being on the fourth day, because of the word concerning them, are said to have come into being since they are greater. For the four, being in power ten, is honorable; for ones, and twos, and threes, and fours, having been joined together, they make the ten; for through all the Scripture the ten...
